scenes.text: What's the difference between Apple's M five Ultra Mac Studio, with eighty GPU cores, and NVIDIA's RTX fifty-eighty, with over ten thousand? How is Apple even competing?
Because Apple's cores are bigger than you think. Each one packs a hundred and twenty-eight math units, but NVIDIA counts every unit as a core. So the totals are nearly identical.
So why is NVIDIA still more powerful? They are built for opposite goals.
NVIDIA builds for maximum output, with a whole chip just for graphics. Apple builds for efficiency, sharing one chip with the CPU.
But Apple's secret weapon is memory. NVIDIA's best gaming card has thirty-two gigabytes. A Mac Studio can share up to five hundred and twelve.
So AI models too big for any gaming card run on a Mac.
NVIDIA is a Ferrari, and Apple is a moving truck. Send this to someone who thinks more cores means faster.
